cases.title: Arm stiff, fingers stiff
cases.what: Arm: today's board gains on the qdd_light build. Fingers: hand-ladder's servo (kp 20 N.m/rad, kd 0.08) at scale 1, closing 15 mm past the block (the 0.65 N.m cap sets the squeeze). Touch peak 44 / 38 N (rigid / soft), arm flange 31 / 26 N, press 16 / 13 N; grasp held (140 mm up) / held (140 mm up). Each tip lands with about the contact's own B v = 40 N: a fingertip is ~0.1 kg either way, and the slap reaches the arm through the joints' bearings (the rotors react at the pivots), 31 N at the flange.

cases.title: Arm stiff, fingers soft
cases.what: Arm: today's board gains on the qdd_light build. Fingers: fingertip impedance, 100 N/m in x / y / z at each tip (impedance_command with the tip's 6x2 Jacobian, HOST_SPRING: the exact spring from the host, the damper on the board; JOINT mode's diagonal rendered a skewed spring that drove the tips into the belt), the same closing reference plus a 5 N inward squeeze feed-forward. Touch peak 44 / 40 N* (rigid / soft), arm flange 27 / 27 N*, press 7.9 / 7.6 N*; grasp dropped (-0 mm up) / dropped (-0 mm up). * flagged: the soft fingertips chatter on the belt and their contact-loss count does not settle by 128 kHz; every force, the rise and the grasp outcome agree within ~3 % from 32 to 128 kHz. Soft fingers halve the press (16 -> 7.9 N) but behind a stiff arm they run out of travel: the 25 mm of overtravel folds them 43 mm, 12 deg into their stops, and they cannot close on the block - the grasp fails. The arm has to hold back within the fingers' deflection budget.

cases.title: Arm soft z, fingers soft
cases.what: Arm: HOST_SPRING, K = (3000, 3000, 500 N/m; 150 N.m/rad), zeta 1. Fingers: fingertip impedance, 100 N/m in x / y / z at each tip (impedance_command with the tip's 6x2 Jacobian, HOST_SPRING: the exact spring from the host, the damper on the board; JOINT mode's diagonal rendered a skewed spring that drove the tips into the belt), the same closing reference plus a 5 N inward squeeze feed-forward. Touch peak 45 / 36 N* (rigid / soft), arm flange 33 / 25 N*, press 7.6 / 8.0 N*; grasp held (107 mm up) / held (107 mm up). * flagged: the soft fingertips chatter on the belt and their contact-loss count does not settle by 128 kHz; every force, the rise and the grasp outcome agree within ~3 % from 32 to 128 kHz. Make the arm soft in z behind them and the same soft fingers keep the low press (7.6 N) and grasp: the arm gives the overtravel back and the fingers keep enough travel to close. The design: the fingers are the soft, light element that sets the press; the arm stays stiff in x/y and soft only in z, so its overtravel never exceeds the fingers' budget (still tight here: 4 deg into a stop at 25 mm of overtravel, and the close snaps them off the stops - press spikes to 168 N against 87 N with stiff fingers; less overtravel or more finger travel is the fix).

cases.title: Arm soft z, fingers stiff
cases.what: Arm: HOST_SPRING, K = (3000, 3000, 500 N/m; 150 N.m/rad), zeta 1. Fingers: hand-ladder's servo (kp 20 N.m/rad, kd 0.08) at scale 1, closing 15 mm past the block (the 0.65 N.m cap sets the squeeze). Touch peak 55 / 51 N (rigid / soft), arm flange 41 / 38 N, press 12 / 12 N; grasp held (135 mm up) / held (135 mm up). Stiff fingers on the soft-z arm grasp too (held (135 mm up)) and are the robust fallback, but press 12 N against 7.6 N with soft fingers, and the tips' slap reaches the flange at 41 N - no split removes the slap itself (the ladder's R1: slow the last centimetres).
